_comment: Touch controls. Sizes are dp, measured from the named screen corner (tl, tr, bl, br) or the top centre (tc) to the element's centre. A copy named touch_layout.json in the game's data folder (Android/data/<package>/files/SO3EE9/) is used instead of this one, so it can be tuned without a new APK. D-pad left, stick bottom left, the face buttons right: the cluster mirrors the stick (anchor mirror: the stick's resting place reflected across the screen, x and y in dp right and down from that point; A sits there, slightly toward the corner), and an element with an arc {of, angle, dist} is put around the element it names (angle in degrees, up is 90; dist in dp, centre to centre) at a spot found from the game's real picture rectangle in this window (16:9 as the game is set up, or the whole window when the picture is stretched), so on a 20:9 phone B, Z and C sit mostly in the black bar. picture.avoid lists the game's HUD as picture fractions [left, top, right, bottom] that the arc buttons keep clear of: the clock bar (the item slots are not listed: the mirrored cluster position is preferred over keeping clear of them). The player's own layout (touch_layout_user.json in the same folder, written by the in-game layout editor) is applied on top of this file: positions as fractions of the window, sizes as factors. A button that does not fit is turned toward straight up and pushed outward. A D-pad arm is offset on the screen (up is up) whatever corner it is measured from. A copy in the game's data folder replaces this file, so an older copy keeps the old places. Buttons are named as the Wii's: a b one two plus minus home up down left right c z.
